assigned.title: Continue watching: resume where the viewer left off
assigned.acceptance: A viewer sees what they were watching and resumes it at the right position. The progress API, its lease route and its writer-epoch conflict rules are complete, tested and reviewed, and no rail, no card progress bar and no resume prompt exists. REQUIRED: a continue-watching rail on home, profile-scoped, ordered by recency, excluding finished items by a stated rule rather than a magic threshold buried in a component. REQUIRED: a progress indicator on cards for partially watched titles. REQUIRED: resume uses the stored position through the session's startAtSeconds, which the playback path already carries, rather than seeking after load -- the test matrix already lists 'resumed playback uses stored progress safely' as a regression scenario. REQUIRED: a viewer can start over; a resume that cannot be declined is a trap.
assigned.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict.

typecheck.evidence: npm run typecheck at a8aa32f: turbo, 22 tasks, 22 successful, exit 0. npm run lint: 12 tasks, exit 0. npm run build: exit 0. THE TYPECHECK IS LOAD-BEARING ON TWO OF THIS TASK'S CHANGES RATHER THAN A FORMALITY. First, listContinueWatching joins the repository port as Bound<typeof listContinueWatching>, derived mechanically from the persistence signature rather than restated, so the port cannot drift from @liberty/persistence and the postgres binding, the in-memory implementation and every caller are checked against one declaration. Second, loadPlaybackSession and watchResultFor each gained a DEFAULTED parameter rather than a required one, and tsc is what establishes that every pre-existing call site -- the watch page, the watch suite, and the handler tests -- compiles unchanged. That is the additive claim, checked rather than asserted. Also checked here: the resume point is threaded as DATA through watch-session.ts and never as an import, so that module's import graph is unchanged.

unit.evidence:
npx turbo run test --force at a8aa32f: 22 tasks, 22 successful, exit 0, nothing cached. apps/web is 70 files and 1194 tests, up 42 from the 1152 recorded on PW-0401; every other workspace is unchanged in count.

lib/continue-watching.test.ts (17) asserts the exclusion rules against the EXPORTED CONSTANTS rather than against literals, because a test that hardcoded 90 and 0.95 would pass after somebody changed the policy and forgot the test. It covers both directions of the two-rule design -- a case the tail catches and the fraction would have kept, and a case the fraction catches and the tail would have kept -- plus both boundaries, the lease exclusion, the glance exclusion, the unknown-runtime case, and the order-preservation and rights-gate properties of the selection.

ONE OF THOSE TESTS WAS WRONG AND THE CODE WAS NOT. The 'one second short of both rules' case first used a two-hour runtime, where 91 seconds from the end is 98.7% through -- the fraction had already fired, so the test was asserting nothing about the tail. It now derives a runtime from the constants themselves and asserts the derivation, which is the only range in which that state is reachable.

continue-watching-ui.test.tsx (14) renders with react-dom/server: a card with no resume is byte-for-byte the card the browse surface already had; a card with one draws the bar at the fraction, says the percentage for a reader who cannot see it, hides the bar from assistive technology, offers a link rather than a form, and repeats the title nowhere; an unknown runtime renders no track at all; and ?restart is matched exactly across seven inputs including an array. Three structural rules hold the rail to its design: it renders CatalogCard rather than a copy, it returns null rather than a state panel, and app/page.tsx mounts it in its own Suspense with fallback={null} -- with a non-vacuity check that the catalog's boundary still has its skeleton.

in-memory-repository.test.ts gained 5 cases, written because the port's own header says an unexecuted implementation is a guess about behaviour: the lease exclusion, the total order with a same-instant tie-break, profile scoping across two profiles of one household, the limit, and the limit refusal.

scope-forgery.test.ts gained the new method, AND ITS EXHAUSTIVENESS ASSERTION DID ITS JOB: adding listContinueWatching to the port failed that suite twice -- once until the method was classified as scope-taking, once until the count was updated -- which is exactly the guard the file exists to be.

watch-session.test.ts gained 5 resume cases: the stored position fills a null, the issuer wins when it states one, nothing stored is the engine default, the parameter defaults so every existing caller is unchanged, and the position arrives on the session rather than as a seek.

ONE GUARD FIRED DURING THIS WORK AND WAS RIGHT TO. build-target.test.ts walks the import graph with a regex over raw source, and a sentence in one of my comments ended with the two characters that regex reads as the start of an import specifier -- so the walk tried to resolve a fragment of English as a module and the section-8 guard failed. The prose moved rather than the walker: a cleverer regex is one that can miss a real import, and that file belongs to a task that owns it.

e2e.evidence:
EXECUTED at a8aa32f, both modes, from e2e/, in the CI job's own configuration -- PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH and PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD unset so the pinned chromium 1234 resolves from Playwright's default cache, CI=1, CONTENT_RIGHTS_ENFORCEMENT=strict, LIBERTY_FC_SEED=20250819, LIBERTY_FIXTURE_MEDIA_ORIGIN=https://fixtures.invalid. Production: 61 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed, exit 0. Development: 70 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed, exit 0. Both counts IDENTICAL to rounds 82 through 90, which is the regression evidence this task most needs: it adds a rail above the catalog on the home route, a second control to the card every rail and the search results render, and a parameter to the watch page -- three of the four surfaces the critical-journey and search specs walk. A moved count would have meant one of them changed shape.

WHAT THIS GATE DOES NOT COVER, STATED PLAINLY. No Playwright spec exercises the continue-watching journey itself. e2e/** is outside this task's allowedPaths, and PW-0303 set the precedent for saying so rather than widening a surface to buy a spec. The rail is also genuinely awkward for that harness as it stands: it requires a profile to be created and selected and progress to be written before the page is loaded, which is three API calls of setup the existing fixtures have no vocabulary for.

WHAT REPLACES IT, AND IT IS STRONGER THAN A SPEC AGAINST FIXTURES. The whole feature was witnessed against a REAL POSTGRESQL 16 -- the instance this container's PW-0401 work created, migrated with the repository's own 0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql -- with next dev supplying the development catalog and DATABASE_URL supplying the store, which is the only combination in which both halves are real at once.

Four progress rows were written through the application's own progress API, one per rule branch: deep-current 2400/3120, aurora-fall 1800/7680, northstar 7150/7200, signal-zero 5/6840. Observed on the rendered home page: the rail is present with the heading 'Continue watching'; its cards are deep-current then aurora-fall, which is recency order; the bars are width:77% and width:23%; the hidden text reads '77% watched' and '23% watched'; the start-over links are /watch/deep-current?restart=1 and /watch/aurora-fall?restart=1; the posters resolve through PW-0302's artwork boundary. northstar does NOT appear -- 50 seconds from the end is inside the 90-second tail -- and signal-zero does NOT appear, at 5 seconds. No progress markup appears anywhere in the catalog rails below.

Resume, observed in the session the watch route server-rendered: /watch/deep-current issues startAtSeconds 2400; ?restart=1 issues null; ?restart=0 and ?restart=true BOTH still issue 2400, which is the exact-match rule rather than a presence check; a title with no progress issues null; the FINISHED title issues null rather than 7150, so a viewer who opens it gets the film and not the credits; the glance issues null.

Profile scoping, observed: creating a second profile and selecting it removes the rail entirely and leaks none of the first profile's titles, and the same watch route then issues null for a title the first profile was half-way through.

ONE FINDING FROM THE WITNESS, REPORTED BECAUSE IT WILL COST SOMEBODY AN HOUR. The first attempt ran next dev with NO database, on the in-memory adapter, and the rail never appeared even though the progress API read its own writes back correctly. The cause is not this feature: lib/db/index.ts memoises the repository in a module-scope variable, and under next dev the React Server Components layer and the route-handler layer are separate compilations of that module -- so a page render and a route handler hold two different in-memory stores. Anything server-rendered from data written through a route handler is invisible in that configuration. It is a development-only artifact of the in-memory adapter, it predates this task, and it is not fixed here; it is named so the next person to test continue watching in next dev does not conclude the feature is broken.

recommended.title: Authentication entry and session UX
recommended.acceptance: A viewer who is signed out can do something about it. PW-0403 made a deployment answer 401 not_authenticated, and there is no screen anywhere in this application that consumes it: /api/auth/* is served and nothing links to it, so the honest description of a deployment today is that it refuses everybody correctly and offers them nowhere to go. REQUIRED: a sign-in screen reachable FROM the signed-out protected state, not only from a URL somebody knows. A 401 that renders as a generic error is the same dead end with better manners. REQUIRED: a sign-up flow where deployment policy permits it. Policy, not preference: requireEmailVerification and the absence of a mail transport both decide what can actually complete, and the screen must reflect what this deployment can do rather than what the library can. REQUIRED: a sign-out action, and an authenticated shell state -- the shell already carries the active profile badge from PW-0303, and who you are SIGNED IN AS is a different fact from which profile is selected. Both belong there and neither may be mistaken for the other. REQUIRED: a protected-view redirect or an equivalent actionable signed-out experience. Either is acceptable; what is not is a screen that silently renders empty because every request behind it returned 401. REQUIRED: verification and password-reset entry states. REQUIRED: EXPLICIT UX WHEN THE MAIL TRANSPORT IS UNAVAILABLE, and this is the clause most likely to be got wrong. The composition root's transport REJECTS rather than logging the link, because a verification or reset URL is a one-click account-takeover token; the screen must say the message cannot be sent and must NOT log, display, copy or otherwise expose such a token to work around it. A UI that showed the link to be helpful would undo the reason the placeholder throws. REQUIRED: it consumes /api/auth/* and does not invent a second auth protocol. No client-side session parsing, no second cookie, no parallel identity state -- the server is the authority and the screen reads its answers. REQUIRED: profile selection is NOT moved into Better Auth. Profiles live above auth (PL-0402), active_profile_selection stays keyed by session in Liberty's own store, and a sign-in screen is exactly where somebody would be tempted to fold the two together. REQUIRED: the server-side not_authenticated behaviour and the PW-0402 authorization boundaries are preserved. Nothing in this task may make a refusal more informative than it is today: the four session failure modes stay externally indistinguishable, and profile_unavailable keeps answering for both of its cases. MEASURED STARTING POINT: apps/web contains no sign-in, sign-up, sign-out or password-reset screen, no link to /api/auth anywhere, and exactly one client-side caller of this application's own API -- the profiles client PW-0303 introduced, whose rules this task should follow rather than re-derive. ADDED ON gpt-architect's ROUND-90 RULING, WHICH GAVE THIS TASK OWNERSHIP OF A GAP PW-0401 FOUND AND WAS FORBIDDEN TO FIX. PW-0401 built the authenticated playback backend; it answers 401 not_authenticated to a signed-out caller, and the desktop forwarder maps that to a generic unavailable because playbackSessionReasonCodeSchema is a CLOSED vocabulary with no authentication member and the response status in that contract is derived from the OUTCOME alone. The ruling: do not expand PW-0401 to solve it, because it is a published-contract concern; PW-0312 owns or coordinates the corrective. REQUIRED: signed-out playback produces an ACTIONABLE SIGN-IN STATE rather than a generic unavailability, on the desktop target as well as the web one. REQUIRED: the distinction between not_authenticated and backend-or-provider unavailability is PRESERVED and not collapsed -- the same ruling PW-0403 received for the request-context vocabulary. REQUIRED: content existence is still not leaked before authentication; PW-0401's ordering property, that the caller is authenticated before the request body is consumed, must survive whatever shape this takes. REQUIRED: if a new playback-session reason code or envelope state is needed, the PUBLISHED CONTRACT IS UPDATED DELIBERATELY FIRST under invariant 5 -- contract.ts, the status derivation and docs/API_CONTRACTS.md together -- rather than a client inferring authentication state from an unavailable. REQUIRED: BOTH TARGETS AND THE CROSS-TARGET EQUIVALENCE TESTS ARE UPDATED TOGETHER. e2e compares whole bodies between the web and desktop targets, so a contract change landing on one target alone is a failing suite at best and a silent divergence at worst. REQUIRED: profile selection stays ABOVE account authentication, unchanged -- this clause already appears above and is restated because a playback-path sign-in prompt is a second place somebody would be tempted to fold the two together.
recommended.notes: Created on gpt-architect's round-85 ruling, which specified the id PW-0310. THAT ID WAS ALREADY TAKEN by 'Keyboard, focus and accessibility across the whole application', filed in round 80 and still BACKLOG, so this task was filed as PW-0312 rather than renumbering or overwriting an existing record. The reviewer also ruled explicitly that this must NOT be folded into PW-0309 (offline, degraded and error states). allowedPaths name directories that do not exist yet; per the PW-0102 surface note, a genuinely new surface is the smallest set the acceptance can be satisfied within and is narrowed again from the diff before review. The shell and the profiles components are reviewDependencies rather than writable: this task will almost certainly need to add a signed-in control to the shell, and that widening should be argued for with a derivation at claim time the way PW-0303's was, not reserved speculatively now. ROUND 90: gpt-architect assigned this task the authentication corrective for the playback path, found by PW-0401 and explicitly out of scope for it. The five added REQUIRED clauses are transcribed from that ruling. This task now spans a published-contract change, so its surface at claim time will be wider than the three directories declared here and the widening must be derived from the acceptance and recorded before it is taken.

recommended.title: Watchlist becomes usable: an add control and a list
recommended.acceptance: A person can add a title to their watchlist and see the list. The API and its mutation rules are complete, tested and reviewed -- including the conflict semantics in packages/persistence/src/watchlist-mutation.ts -- and nothing renders them. REQUIRED: the add control appears on the title screen and on a catalog card, and reflects state optimistically while remaining correct when the write is refused. REQUIRED: the resolution vocabulary the API already returns (accepted plus a reason, not a boolean ok) is surfaced honestly; a refused write must not render as a success, which is the shape of defect the harnesses in this repository have caught four times.

recommended.title: Offline, degraded and error states a desktop application needs
recommended.acceptance: The application behaves honestly when the network, the backend or the sidecar is unavailable. There is no offline handling of any kind today -- no navigator.onLine, no service worker, no offline banner, no retry-on-reconnect. THIS MATTERS MORE ON THE DESKTOP THAN IT DID ON THE WEB: docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 8 accepts that an offline desktop cannot resolve playback at all, and requires that failure be surfaced as an honest unavailable outcome rather than an empty candidate list -- so the UI half of that ruling is this task. REQUIRED: a network-state signal and a visible degraded mode that names what is unavailable. REQUIRED: recovery on reconnect without a manual reload. REQUIRED: the sidecar being down is a DISTINCT state from the backend being down and from the network being down, because the three have different remedies and collapsing them produces a support burden. REQUIRED: no state invents content; an offline home shows what it has and says so.
